sections.h2: How fast can a Lancaster house sell, and which route is best?
sections.html:
The route you choose sets the pace in Lancaster. An agent listing takes the longest because of showings and a buyer's loan, a by-owner sale moves at the pace you can manage, and a cash buyer can close once title work is clear.

  • Agent sale: right for a house that shows well and an owner with patience.
  • Owner sale: trims the fee and adds tasks, from the disclosure form to the deed packet.
  • Cash sale: made for inherited houses, rentals and homes whose repair list outruns the budget.

Lancaster is a growing city of about 18.85 square miles. Its population reached 41,956 in mid 2025, 3.5 percent more than the 40,543 counted in April 2020, and 59.1 percent of households own their home. Older houses near downtown sit beside newer subdivisions on the edges. Many workers drive toward Columbus, about 33 miles northwest.

Modest prices and family-sized households make this a town where owner-occupant buyers are common, and children under 18 make up 22.7 percent of residents.

Lancaster City Schools serve the city, with Lancaster High School as the public high school, and Ohio University Lancaster operates a branch campus. Health care, glass and government anchor the job market, led by Fairfield Medical Center and Anchor Hocking. The city's nickname is Glass City, and downtown has the Ohio Glass Museum.

Old houses mean old systems, so keep receipts for roof, furnace and water heater work and hand them to the buyer with the disclosure form. Winters and summers here put real demands on heating, pipes, cooling and attic ventilation, and buyers know it.

If the house you are selling is rented by the night, the city's rules matter. Lancaster's zoning code includes a Short Term Rentals chapter, 1131, which council took up in a 2025 ordinance. Check the current text with the city's Community Development Department.

  • Definition: a dwelling with up to five guestrooms, rented for stays under 30 days in a row.
  • Permit: a zoning clearance permit is required for each short term rental, renewed every two years, with a renewal deadline of the first Monday in November of the year the permit expires.
  • Local host: the host must be able to respond to an emergency within one hour.
  • Occupancy permit: the Building Department issues one before the first rental.

A change in ownership voids the current permit and calls for a new application. Any buyer who wants to keep renting the house by the night will have to apply again, so say so at the first showing.

sections.h2: Fairfield County Auditor and the deed
sections.html:
As the Fairfield County seat, Lancaster has the County Auditor's office right in town, at 108 N. High Street, and the doors close to filers at four in the afternoon. The transfer fee is $.50 per parcel, and the conveyance fee is $4.00 per thousand of consideration when money changes hands.

  • Legal description first: the prepared deed goes to the Auditor's Map Room, by email at maproom@fairfieldcountyohio.gov, for approval before the transfer desk accepts it.
  • Documents: a deed and a DTE 100 conveyance fee statement, or a DTE 100 EX for exempt transfers.
  • Delivery: in person, by mail to Attn: Conveyance, or electronically through Simplifile.
  • Recording: afterward, the Fairfield County Recorder, at (740) 652-7100, records the deed.

Ohio Revised Code 319.202 puts the fee on the seller and requires the buyer to submit the value statement.

Ohio Revised Code 5302.30 calls for the disclosure form on residential property of up to four units. Its exceptions cover estate fiduciary transfers and inherited property the seller has not lived in for a year. If neither fits, complete the form even for an as-is sale. A financed buyer may ask for repairs after an inspection, while a cash buyer builds them into the price.

sections.h2: Should a Lancaster seller choose a cash buyer?
sections.html:
Cash earns a look when a conventional sale would stall over repairs, a cloudy title or a tight deadline. In Lancaster that often describes a house with old mechanical systems, a rental with tenants, or an estate with several heirs.

Get a written offer that names the closing date and says who pays title and recording costs. Compare the Auditor's fee against the closing statement, and keep the signed disclosure form in your own file. Offers from two or three buyers, plus an agent's estimate of net proceeds, will show whether the speed is worth the discount.

sections.h2: What a cash sale skips, and what it does not
sections.html:
A cash sale skips the buyer's loan approval, the lender's appraisal and the round of repair requests that often follows a financed buyer's inspection. It does not skip the county. The deed still goes through the Map Room, the Auditor's desk and the Recorder, and the disclosure form still applies unless you qualify for an exemption.

That is worth knowing because the slowest part of many Lancaster sales is not the buyer at all. A deed with an unapproved legal description, a missing DTE 100 or a fee paid after the office closes can cost a day or two. Ask the title company to confirm each document before it heads to High Street, and ask it whether it will carry the deed in for you.

If the house is an estate property with several heirs, agree among yourselves who signs, who receives the proceeds and who speaks to the buyer. Sorting that out early is often the difference between a quick closing and a stalled one.

Whoever delivers the deed should bring the deed itself, the DTE 100 conveyance fee statement or the DTE 100 EX for an exempt transfer, and the exact fee. The Auditor takes filings in person, by mail to Attn: Conveyance, or electronically through Simplifile. After the Auditor approves it, the Fairfield County Recorder at (740) 652-7100 records the deed, and you can call that office with questions about recording.

sections.h2: Getting a Lancaster sale to the finish
sections.html:
A short sequence keeps the deed from stalling at the county.

  1. Decide the route and, for a nightly rental, tell the buyer the permit ends with your ownership.
  2. Sign and deliver the disclosure form unless an exemption applies.
  3. Have the deed drafted and send the legal description to the Map Room for approval.
  4. Complete the DTE 100, or the DTE 100 EX when the transfer is exempt, and pay the fees before four in the afternoon.
  5. Let the Recorder file the deed once the Auditor has approved it.

faqs.q: How much is the Fairfield County conveyance fee on a Lancaster house?
faqs.a: The fee is $4.00 per thousand of consideration plus a $.50 per parcel transfer fee. Ohio Revised Code 319.202 makes the grantor responsible.

faqs.q: Where does a Lancaster deed get dropped off?
faqs.a: The Fairfield County Auditor's transfer desk at 108 N. High Street takes it once the Map Room approves the legal description. Standard weekday hours run until 4:00 p.m.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Lancaster home as is?
faqs.a: Yes, but you still complete the Ohio disclosure form that Revised Code 5302.30 requires for homes of up to four units. A financed buyer may ask for repairs after an inspection, while a cash buyer builds them into the price.

faqs.q: Does a nightly rental permit carry over to a Lancaster buyer?
faqs.a: No. The city's short term rental chapter says a change in ownership voids the current zoning clearance permit and requires a new application. Confirm the current rules with the city's Community Development Department.

faqs.q: What is the typical commute from Lancaster?
faqs.a: Workers in Lancaster average 27.7 minutes to get to their jobs. Columbus sits about 33 miles northwest of the city.
